- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum (e.g., sentiment change > -0.67 or news volume drops to 0), reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines sharply (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment changes), model overestimates future upside; adjust forecast downward by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When news volume drops to 0 for 2+ consecutive days, suppress forecast momentum; assume price will revert to 1–2-day moving average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently overpredicts by >2% over 3–5 prior days, apply a 1–2% downward bias to correct for lagged sentiment misalignment.
